leads_to.evidence: BLS lists a bachelor's degree as the usual entry education for market research analysts, with no license required. Some employers prefer a master's degree, and many new graduates start in entry roles such as marketing assistant.

nearby_pair.evidence: Both programs take students straight from high school. At FIT, freshmen start in the two-year associate degree and then move up to the bachelor's. Berkeley College admits freshmen directly into its four-year marketing communications BBA.

school_matters.evidence: Top undergraduate business schools send most graduates to finance and consulting, and marketing is one of several smaller destinations. Only a few schools have marketing programs in the top admission bands, so most marketing graduates compete in the ordinary job market.

who_is_counted.evidence: The schools that award the most marketing degrees are large public universities such as the University of Alabama, which mostly enroll first-time students. None of the largest programs is online-only or pooled.

programs.evidence: Wharton is a highly selective undergraduate business school. Its graduates are recruited mainly by banks and consulting firms, and big consumer brands also recruit there.
Georgetown's McDonough is a selective business school. Most of its undergraduates go into financial services and consulting, and marketing and advertising are smaller destinations.
WashU's Olin is a selective business school. Its BSBA graduates are hired mostly into finance and consulting, at salaries well above typical business pay.
